ridings.name: Bulkley Valley-Stikine
ridings.communities: Smithers, Telkwa, Hazelton, New Hazelton, Stewart, Dease Lake, Atlin, Kispiox, Kitwanga, Gitanyow, Moricetown

candidates.name: Frankie Abel
candidates.bio: Gitxsan mother and advisor who grew up in northern B.C. Has worked in cultural safety, Indigenous governance and public policy, most recently for a provincial Crown corporation. First-time candidate.

candidates.name: Ed Ewald
candidates.bio: Works in retail at a local hardware store after farm and sawmill jobs and over 20 years on a dairy farm. President of CHP-BC. Replaces Rod Taylor as candidate.

candidates.name: Sharon Hartwell
candidates.bio: Born and raised in the Bulkley Valley. Telkwa councillor, then mayor from 1995 to 2009. MLA since 2024. Lived in Alberta for eight years before her 2023 nomination.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on Elections BC list as of Oct 12, 2026. No Green, CentreBC or OneBC candidate. Hartwell won the seat from Nathan Cullen (NDP) in 2024. Rod Taylor (CHP, 2024) is not on the ballot.

ridings.name: Cariboo-Chilcotin
ridings.communities: Williams Lake, 100 Mile House, Clinton, Ashcroft, Cache Creek, Anahim Lake, Alexis Creek, Canim Lake, Lac la Hache, Forest Grove, Horsefly area
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: No party change by the MLA since the 2024 election. Lorne Doerkson (elected 2020 as BC Liberal/BC United, joined the Conservatives in 2024 before the election) became interim leader of the Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in September 2026 after Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigned on Sept 20, 2026.

candidates.name: Kathryn Askew
candidates.bio: Retired teacher with 32 years in education and past local president and bargaining chair of her teachers' union. Lives at Canim Lake; volunteers with the Hawkins Lake fire department.

candidates.name: Lorne Doerkson
candidates.bio: Interim Conservative leader and Cariboo-Chilcotin MLA since 2020. Spent 20 years as a Black Press newspaper publisher, then worked in financial planning; has lived in the Cariboo for close to 30 years.

sources.label: Conservative Party of BC: Lorne Doerkson
Global News: who are the BC party leaders (2026)

candidates.name: Douglas Gook
candidates.bio: Ran for the BC Greens in Cariboo North in 2020 (707 votes, 6.4 percent) and in Nechako Lakes in 2024 (622 votes, 5.3 percent), per Elections BC. The party lists him as its 2026 candidate without a biography.
candidates.note: No bio on bcgreens.ca/candidates-2026 (listed without a profile link). Bio built from past candidacies only.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on Elections BC list. Doerkson is confirmed as MLA for Cariboo-Chilcotin and interim Conservative leader (Wikipedia, Doerkson page).

ridings.name: Nechako Lakes
ridings.communities: Vanderhoof, Fort St. James, Burns Lake, Houston, Fraser Lake, Granisle, Endako, Fort Fraser, Southside (Francois and Ootsa lakes)
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: John Rustad (MLA, Conservative) was removed as party leader on Dec 3, 2025, was removed from the Conservative caucus on Sept 18, 2026 and rejoined on Sept 21, 2026. He announced he will not run again; the seat is open and no sitting MLA is on the ballot.

candidates.name: Diane Black
candidates.bio: Vanderhoof-born accountant with an MBA, from a multi-generation farm family. Has held a senior finance role at Nicola Valley Institute of Technology. No prior elected office.

candidates.name: Jesse Gervais
candidates.bio: Fraser Lake municipal administrator (community services, deputy corporate officer). Sits on the UNBC board of governors and the Fraser Lake Community Foundation; has held Metis Nation elected office.

candidates.name: Clint Lambert
candidates.bio: Burns Lake Southside rancher and business owner. Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako director for Electoral Area E since 2018; president of the Lakes District Cattlemen's Association.
candidates.note: Runs as a self-described 'blue independent'. Absent from the older Elections BC CSV snapshot (and the coordinator's candidates_min.json) but present on the Elections BC web list and PDF of Oct 12, 2026.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on the current Elections BC list (the CSV snapshot shows only 2). Rustad's non-running is reported by CTV (https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/former-bc-conservative-leader-john-rustad-not-seeking-re-election/); the Wikipedia incumbents table gives Dec 4, 2025 as the date, which conflicts with local reports of Sept 23, 2026. No Green, CentreBC or OneBC candidate.

ridings.name: North Coast-Haida Gwaii
ridings.communities: Prince Rupert, Port Edward, Haida Gwaii (Masset, Daajing Giids, Port Clements, Sandspit), Lax Kw'alaams, Metlakatla, Bella Bella, Bella Coola, Klemtu, Hartley Bay

candidates.name: Tamara Davidson
candidates.bio: MLA since 2024 and former Minister of Environment and Parks. Haida name Laanas. Previously on the Council of the Haida Nation and a federal public servant.

candidates.name: Rodney Proskiw
candidates.bio: Prince Rupert small business owner who has lived there 20 years. Past president of the Prince Rupert Lions Club and longest-serving former director of Tourism Prince Rupert.

candidates.name: Francis Racy
candidates.bio: Leads mental health education programming for educators across the northwest. Past health care assistant and early childhood educator; chairs the Powell River BCSPCA Community Council.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on Elections BC list. No OneBC or CentreBC candidate. The former MLA before 2024 was Jennifer Rice (NDP), who did not run in 2024.

ridings.name: Peace River North
ridings.communities: Fort St. John, Fort Nelson, Hudson's Hope, Taylor, Northern Rockies, Charlie Lake, Wonowon, Pink Mountain
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Jordan Kealy (elected as a Conservative in 2024) left the Conservative caucus on March 7, 2025 and has sat as an independent since. He was charged with one count of sexual assault on June 3, 2026 and has said he is innocent (Energeticcity, June 4, 2026).

candidates.name: Jordan Kealy
candidates.bio: Farmer and mechanic. Peace River Regional District director 2022 to 2024. Elected MLA in 2024 as a Conservative, left that caucus in March 2025 and sits as an independent.
candidates.note: Faces one count of sexual assault (charged June 3, 2026; headed to a jury trial). He has said he is innocent. The charge is unproven.

candidates.name: Curtis Whitford
candidates.bio: Fort St. John area resident with 36 years in oil and gas, from oilfield construction to regional manager. Joined a local co-operative board; coached and served on minor hockey boards.

ridings.notes: 2 candidates on Elections BC list. The BC NDP did not nominate a candidate (reported incomplete paperwork, per Wikipedia and Daily Hive). Dan Davies (2024 independent) is not running.

ridings.name: Peace River South
ridings.communities: Dawson Creek, Chetwynd, Tumbler Ridge, Pouce Coupe, Moberly Lake, Groundbirch, Tomslake

candidates.name: Marsha Rose Dufresne
candidates.bio: Longtime Indigenous education support worker. Past director of Tumbler Ridge Community Forests and the Tumbler Ridge UNESCO Global Geopark. Volunteer and grandmother.

candidates.name: Larry Neufeld
candidates.bio: Engineer who founded his own company in 2006 and is a former reserve infantry platoon commander. Raised in northern Saskatchewan. MLA since 2024; Conservative natural gas and LNG critic.

candidates.name: Helen Scott
candidates.bio: Unaffiliated candidate. Elections BC lists a Tumbler Ridge mailing address for her. No further biography found.
candidates.note: No biographical source found. Bio limited to what Elections BC and Energeticcity state.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on Elections BC list. The older CSV labelled Scott 'Other'; the web list says Unaffiliated. 2024 independent Mike Bernier is not running.

ridings.name: Prince George-Mackenzie
ridings.communities: Prince George (College Heights, Hart Highlands, University Heights, Pinewood area), Mackenzie, McLeod Lake, Bear Lake, Summit Lake

candidates.name: Kiel Giddens
candidates.bio: Prince George resident. Former Coastal GasLink public affairs manager, past president of the Prince George Chamber of Commerce and former ministerial chief of staff. MLA since 2024.

candidates.name: Ian McMahon
candidates.bio: Public servant with three decades in B.C. government, Parliament Hill and the Canadian Embassy in Washington. Has taught political science. NDP candidate in Peace River North in 2024.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Results of the 2024 British Columbia general election by riding

candidates.name: Teri Young
candidates.bio: Retired teacher who taught in New Aiyansh and ran a software distribution company for over 30 years until 2018. Volunteers with Cowichan Hospice and a watershed group.
candidates.note: Green bio mentions Cowichan volunteer work. A Teri Young also ran for the Greens in Skeena in 2024; identity not confirmed.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on Elections BC list. McMahon's 2024 candidacy is per Wikipedia's 2024 candidate table.

ridings.name: Prince George-North Cariboo
ridings.communities: Prince George (north and west parts), Quesnel, Wells, Barkerville, Bouchie Lake, Nazko, Likely, Horsefly, Blackwater
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: No party change. Sheldon Clare became Opposition House Leader in 2026.

candidates.name: Denice Bardua
candidates.bio: Quesnel resident since 1997 who works in education. Active in the Bouchie Lake community and in her union. NDP candidate in this riding in 2024.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Results of the 2024 British Columbia general election by riding

candidates.note: Spelled 'Denice' by Elections BC and the NDP; some media print 'Denise'.

candidates.name: Sheldon Clare
candidates.bio: Born and raised in Prince George. College of New Caledonia history instructor since 1993, past national president of the National Firearms Association, Legion Branch 43 president. MLA since 2024.

candidates.name: Randy Thompson
candidates.bio: Quesnel farmer and small-business owner (Oddball Garlic Company) who works for the City of Quesnel. Green candidate here in 2024; served two years on the party's Provincial Council.

ridings.notes: 3 candidates on Elections BC list. Independent Coralee Oakes (2024, 21.8 percent) is not running.

ridings.name: Prince George-Valemount
ridings.communities: Prince George (south and east parts), Valemount, McBride, Dunster, Tete Jaune Cache, Blue River, Giscome, Willow River
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Rosalyn Bird (elected as a Conservative in 2024) left the Conservative caucus on Aug 25, 2026 and sat as an independent, joined CentreBC on Sept 18, 2026, and rejoined the Conservatives about four days later (around the election call on Sept 22). She is running as a Conservative.

candidates.name: Rosalyn Bird
candidates.bio: Former Canadian Armed Forces naval logistics officer (service from 1990) with NATO and Afghanistan-related deployments. MLA since 2024 and Conservative critic for Citizens' Services.

candidates.name: Carol Bourque
candidates.bio: Public-sector professional with over 30 years of service, including 14 years in health information management with Northern Health. Born and raised in Prince George; Indigenous woman.

candidates.name: Jodie Capling
candidates.bio: Grew up in the Cariboo-Chilcotin and now lives in Williams Lake. Background in environmental management and energy efficiency; teaches yoga. Previously ran for the Greens federally.
candidates.note: Green bio places her in Williams Lake, outside this riding.

candidates.name: Mitchell Lukoni
candidates.bio: Born and raised in Prince George. Works as a business, communications and policy strategist. Athabasca University degree; past UNBC student senator and hospice grief-support volunteer.

ridings.notes: 4 candidates on Elections BC list; the only 4-way race in the Prince George area.

ridings.name: Skeena
ridings.communities: Terrace, Kitimat, Thornhill, Kitselas, Kitsumkalum, Kitamaat Village, New Aiyansh, Gingolx, Lakelse Lake, Rosswood
ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Claire Rattée (Conservative) was removed from the Conservative caucus on Sept 18, 2026 and rejoined on Sept 21, 2026. She is running as a Conservative.

candidates.name: Nick Gottlieb
candidates.bio: Writer, researcher and community organizer completing a PhD at Simon Fraser University on Canada's LNG industry. Has lived in Terrace about five years; helped found the Skeena Local Action Network.

candidates.name: Claire Rattée
candidates.bio: Kitimat tattoo artist and co-owner of Arcane Arts for over 13 years. Kitimat councillor 2014 to 2018; federal Conservative candidate in 2019 and 2021. MLA since 2024.

candidates.name: Larry Eugene Taylor
candidates.bio: Born and raised in Terrace. Heavy duty mechanic for over 42 years and a Terrace volunteer firefighter for 13 years. Married with five children.
candidates.note: OneBC site lists him as 'Larry Taylor'; the Elections BC ballot name is Larry Eugene Taylor.

candidates.name: Sarah Zimmerman
candidates.bio: Elected Terrace city councillor, former journalist and senior communications leader. Volunteers with Terrace Rotary Club and My Mountain Co-op. NDP candidate in Skeena in 2024.

ridings.notes: 4 candidates on Elections BC list. The 2024 Skeena CHP count is 126 per the Elections BC Statement of Votes (Wikipedia shows 125).
